Theme

Conversation, family & daily routines

there adverb

to that place

also to there, thither, over there

classical

Catull. 3.9: modo hūc modo illūc
Hor. C. 4.11.9–10: hūc et illūc cursitant

illūc

adverb

to there

To a place away from both of us; hūc et illūc, this way and that.

Other words

  • eō — there, thither (to the place named)

    adverb · classical · Cato Agr. 1.2: utī eō introeās et circumspiciās; Caes. BG 1.25.5: eō sē recipere coepērunt; Traupman 360

    The unemphatic “(to) there”; it answers quō. Not the verb eō, I go.

  • istūc — there (to where you are)

    adverb · also used · classical · Ter. Eun. 706: Concēde istūc paululum

Examples

  • utī eō introeās et circumspiciās, utī inde exīre possīs

    go in there and look round, so that you can get out of there againCato Agr. 1.2

  • circumsiliēns modo hūc modo illūc ad sōlam dominam ūsque pīpiābat

    hopping about, now this way, now that, it kept cheeping to its mistress aloneCatull. 3.9–10

  • Concēde istūc paululum: audīn'? etiam nunc paululum: sat est.

    Move over there a little — do you hear? — a little more — that’s enough.Ter. Eun. 706

  • Quō tē agis? — Egone? in aedem Veneris. — Quid eō?

    Where are you off to? — Me? To the temple of Venus. — What are you going there for?Plaut. Poen. 333–333c

  • cūncta festīnat manus, hūc et illūc cursitant mixtae puerīs puellae

    the whole household bustles; girls and boys together run this way and thatHor. C. 4.11.9–10

See also there, here, where to, that way.
